findings.summary: Attention now determines pooled p50. Its current 3.13 s diagnostic call is 90.7% OCR and 5.9% embedding.
observations: The accepted configuration uses four L4 GPUs, server concurrency eight, region window 64, dynamic pages and compiled BF16 embeddings with batch sixteen. This profile uses one warm-up, three ordinary calls and a separate instrumented full-PDF call.
Median OCR time is 2.828 s and embedding is 0.184 s. Mean stage shares are 90.7% OCR, 5.9% embedding, 3.1% rendering and 0.4% chunking.
OCR-window mean GPU busy for GPUs 0–3 is [63.9, 43.7, 67.0, 97.6]%, based on [7, 7, 7, 7] one-second samples. The short capture does not establish peak compute or memory-bandwidth saturation.

Region counts were nearly equal across GPUs (17, 16, 17, 17), but generated-token totals were 913, 454, 854 and 1,510 in every ordinary call. GPU 3 performed 3.3 times GPU 1’s decoding work. Balancing request counts does not balance this document’s token work.

OCR-window peak running requests per GPU are [8.0, 8.0, 7.0, 8.0], peak waiting requests [4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0]. Waiting appears in [15.0, 8.6, 7.5, 22.5]% of scheduler snapshots. The earlier sixteen-request trial did not improve the pooled metrics.
All four bounded traces and the full instrumented output were captured; the frozen reference check passed. Kernel traces cover the first 32 engine iterations only.

The retained Census profile has the same OCR configuration and identifies a 3,252-token page-5 region dominating the tail. Together these studies support testing decoder work, with the five-PDF evaluator checking both short-document p50 and long-document p95.
